content: 1. Estrogens, when administered in high systemic doses, may partially reduce tissue sensitivity to the action of hyaluronidase. This may necessitate higher doses of hyaluronidase to achieve equivalent dispersing effects. Close monitoring is advised. 2. Hydrocortisone can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing the metabolism mediated by the hepatic/intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 3. Idelalisib, a strong CYP3A inhibitor, can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. If unavoidable, monitor closely for increased estrogenic effects. 4. Iloperidone, a time-dependent CYP3A inhibitor, may elevate plasma levels of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This could also increase plasma levels of other drugs metabolized by CYP3A4. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 5. Esterified estrogens may inhibit hepatic metabolism of tricyclic antidepressants (TCAs), potentially increasing TCA plasma concentrations and adverse effects. However, such interactions are uncommon. Close monitoring is advised. 6. Indinavir can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 7. Isoniazid may increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is advised. 8. Istradefylline at 40 mg/day has been shown to increase peak levels and AUC of CYP3A4 substrates in clinical trials, but this effect was not observed at 20 mg/day. Dose reduction of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates may be necessary. Close monitoring is recommended. 9. Itraconazole can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 10. Ivosidenib, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative therapies should be used. If unavoidable, monitor for loss of therapeutic efficacy. 11. Ketoconazole can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 12. Oral estrogens may reduce serum insulin-like growth factor-1 (IGF-1) response to lonapegsomatropin. Patients on oral estrogen replacement may require higher lonapegsomatropin dosages. Close monitoring is necessary. 13. Lopinavir can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 14. Lorlatinib, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Co-administration should be avoided, or alternative drugs should be considered. 15. Esterified estrogens may decrease magnesium levels (e.g., magnesium chloride, citrate, hydroxide, oxide, sulfate) by shifting magnesium from blood to tissue storage. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 16. Maraviroc levels may increase when co-administered with esterified estrogens due to CYP3A4 metabolism effects, potentially leading to increased toxicity. Close monitoring is advised. 17. Meropenem/vaborbactam may decrease the levels or effects of oral esterified estrogens by altering intestinal flora. This interaction poses a low risk of contraceptive failure. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 18. Metyrapone's therapeutic response may be reduced in patients on estrogen therapy. It is generally advisable to discontinue estrogens prior to and during metyrapone administration. Close monitoring is necessary. 19. Miconazole vaginal administration can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 20. Mifepristone can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 21. Mitotane, a strong CYP3A4 inducer, can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Dosage adjustments may be required. Close monitoring is necessary. 22. Mycophenolate may reduce the effects of esterified estrogens through an unknown mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear, but close monitoring is recommended. 23. Nafcillin can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 24. Nefazodone can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 25. Nelfinavir can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 26. Nevirapine can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 27. Ospemifene and esterified estrogens exhibit pharmacodynamic synergism, increasing each other's effects. Co-administration is contraindicated. 28. Oxcarbazepine can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 29. Pentobarbital can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 30. Phenobarbital can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 31. Phenytoin can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. If estrogens are used for contraception, loss of contraceptive efficacy may occur. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 32. Phytoestrogens may reduce the effects of esterified estrogens through pharmacodynamic antagonism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 33. Pleurisy root may reduce the effects of esterified estrogens through an unspecified mechanism. This interaction is theoretical, and its clinical significance is unknown. 34. Posaconazole can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 35. Primidone can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 36. St. John’s Wort can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 37. Stiripentol, a CYP1A2 inhibitor and inducer, may alter the effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Dosage adjustments of CYP1A2 substrates may be required. Close monitoring is necessary. 38. Tacrolimus can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 39. Tazemetostat can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 40. Tecovirimat, a weak CYP3A4 inducer, may reduce the effectiveness of sensitive CYP3A4 substrates, including esterified estrogens. Close monitoring is advised. 41. Teriflunomide can decrease the levels of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP1A2 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 42. Tolvaptan can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Caution and monitoring are advised. 43. Topiramate can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. This may compromise the efficacy of estrogens used for contraception or hormone replacement therapy. Caution and monitoring are necessary. 44. Trazodone and esterified estrogens may interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 45. Trimipramine and esterified estrogens may interact through an unspecified mechanism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 46. Pyridoxine levels may be reduced by esterified estrogens due to altered metabolism. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 47. Quinidine can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Therapy modification and close monitoring are recommended. 48. Quinupristin/dalfopristin can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 49. Ribociclib can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 50. Rifabutin can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 51. Rifampin can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 52. Rifapentine can decrease the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by influencing CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are advised. 53. Ritonavir can increase the levels or effects of esterified estrogens by altering CYP3A4 metabolism. Caution and monitoring are recommended. 54. Rose hips may have reduced levels when co-administered with esterified estrogens due to increased elimination. The clinical significance of this interaction is unclear. 55. Siponimod and esterified estrogens may both increase immunosuppressive effects, raising the risk of infection. Caution is advised during and after co-administration due to additive immunosuppressive effects. 56. Oral estrogens may reduce the serum IGF-1 response to somapacitan, necessitating higher somapacitan dosages. Refer to the drug monograph for starting dose recommendations. Close monitoring is necessary.
